- `paused_tasks` — ids of tasks whose assigned robot currently cannot reach a
  required point on the saved map.
- `traffic_waits` — optional list of `{"robot_id", "blocked_by", "ticks"}`
  entries: robots currently held up by other robots, who blocks them, and for
  how many consecutive ticks. Older files without this field load with every
  counter at zero.
- `map_changes` — every actual edit in order, each
  `{"tick", "sequence", "added", "removed"}`; `sequence` runs from 1 and
  consecutive edits at the same `tick` preserve their order.
- `replay` — ordered events. Tick frames are `{"type": "tick", "tick", "moved",
  "robots", "completed"}`, numbered consecutively from `1` through `tick`.
  Map-change frames are interspersed at their effective tick and have the shape
  `{"type": "map_change", "tick", "sequence", "added", "removed"}`. In any
  non-zero-tick file the last tick frame's robot positions must equal the
  current robot positions; historical frames are never overwritten by later
  maps.

Loading validates the entire document: corrupted JSON, missing or wrongly
typed fields, unsupported versions, duplicate robot or task ids, overlapping
or out-of-bounds/blocked robot positions, routes that leave the map, cross
obstacles unexplained by the change history, make non-adjacent moves, or
cannot complete the robot's bound task, task/robot ownership mismatches, a
broken replay history, out-of-bounds or add/remove-conflicting change
records,
a change history that does not reproduce the saved grid, and an inconsistent
paused-task state are all rejected. So is a replay whose *history* could never
have happened, even when its final frame matches the saved robots: a robot out
of bounds or on an obstacle that existed at that tick, two robots sharing a
cell at a tick boundary, a jump of more than one orthogonal cell or a two-robot
cell swap between neighboring tick frames, and a `moved` list that names an
unknown/duplicated robot or does not exactly match the robots that changed
position (following another robot into the cell it just vacated is legal, and
the list need not be sorted). Map edits are judged against contemporary
positions: a cell a robot once passed through may be closed later without
invalidating the replay, a robot may not appear in a cell before it opens, and
an edit may not add an obstacle onto a cell occupied when that tick ended —
not even if another edit of the same tick removes it again. The first tick
frame has no recorded predecessor, so its cells, overlaps and `moved` ids are
still checked but the first moves are not second-guessed; zero-tick files,
empty fleets and all-waiting frames remain valid. Beyond physical
plausibility, each assigned, unfinished, non-paused task must still be
completable along its robot's remaining route: a non-empty route has to end at
the dropoff, and a robot that has not collected yet — unless it is already
standing on the pickup cell — must still pass through the pickup (visiting the
dropoff early and leaving again is fine; detours need not match a replanned
shortest path). An empty route is accepted only for a loaded robot already at
the dropoff, or when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; map-paused
tasks keep their empty-route exemption. Version 1 documents contain
tick frames without a `type` field and none of the edit-related keys; they
load as if no map edit had ever happened.

The one blocked-waypoint route a version 2 checkpoint accepts belongs to a
robot with no bound task that is waiting out a dynamic closure: the blocked
waypoint must have been traversable on the initial map, a valid map change
must have closed it, and it must still be closed in the saved grid — exactly
the state normal running produces when a preset route reaches a cell that was
later shut. Saving and loading preserve the position, the remaining waypoint
order, the mileage and the change history without advancing time or moving
the robot; on resume the robot finishes the still-open waypoints, waits
without consuming a waypoint or gaining mileage, and continues the original
route from the next cell once the way reopens, never detouring or skipping.
The exemption is narrow: creating a fleet directly still rejects a route
through an initial obstacle, a blocked waypoint that the change history
cannot explain is rejected, task-bound robots keep their reroute/pause rules,
and version 1 files keep the old requirement. A robot standing on an
obstacle, an out-of-map or non-integer waypoint, and a jump between waypoints
are rejected regardless.

1	"""Task assignment, dynamic map edits and collision-aware tick execution.
2	
3	Obstacles may be closed and reopened between ticks through
4	:meth:`FleetSimulator.modify_obstacles`. Every accepted edit is appended to a
5	deterministic change history and mirrored into the replay as a ``map_change``
6	event stamped with the tick at which it took effect. Tick frames themselves are
7	never rewritten, so historical frames keep the positions and completion
8	information recorded at the time.
9	
10	Automatic yielding
11	------------------
12	When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, ``step()`` tries to
13	keep traffic flowing instead of waiting forever: a parked blocker (one with no
14	bound task *and* no remaining route) is asked to move onto a free side cell
15	that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy robot facing a blocker that
16	cannot drive on may itself sidestep onto a free adjacent cell and replan its
17	(still shortest) route from there. A taskless robot that still carries a
18	remaining route is not parked: it drives that route cell by cell exactly like
19	a task-bound robot, is never pushed onto a side cell for someone else, and if
20	its own next cell is blocked it simply keeps its place and its unconsumed
21	waypoints -- an open side cell changes nothing. Only once such a route is
22	exhausted does the robot become a parked robot and yield by the side-cell
23	rule. Task assignment follows the same line: only a robot with no bound task
24	*and* no remaining route can receive a waiting task, so a taskless robot
25	still driving its preset route never has that route overwritten by a new
26	assignment -- being blocked by traffic along the way does not count as having
27	finished the route, and once the route runs out the robot joins the selection
28	at the next assignment pass, planned from wherever it stands then. A retreat that
29	only leads back to the same immovable blocker is never taken though: if the
30	replanned route immediately returns through the vacated cell, still passes the
31	blocker's cell and the blocker cannot use the opening to leave (a dead end or
32	corridor end with traffic parked beyond it), the robot simply waits -- extra
33	empty cells stretching out behind it change nothing. Nor does the blocker's
34	own side step automatically count as leaving: when that step only moves the
35	blocker onto a side cell whose replanned route returns it onto the corridor
36	to face the very same unyielding jam further ahead, the opening is no opening
37	and the retreat behind it is rejected as well. Yield moves count as
38	mileage, waiting does not. The task keeps its original robot, pickup and
39	completion rules are unchanged, and a robot paused by map unreachability never
40	takes part in yielding. If no safe side cell exists the robots simply wait:
41	time advances, nothing collides and nothing completes early. Waiting caused
42	purely by other robots is tracked per robot (consecutive ticks and the
43	blocking robot) and reported by :meth:`FleetSimulator.status` and
44	:meth:`FleetSimulator.metrics` as ``traffic_waits``, distinct from the
45	map-unreachability ``paused_tasks``. The record is judged against the
46	end-of-tick layout, not the moment the robot gave way: when a robot that was
47	asked to wait sees its next cell free at tick end (the blocker drove on or
48	made room later in the same tick), no wait is reported for that tick at all,
49	and ``blocked_by`` names whichever robot actually occupies the cell once the
50	tick settles. The counter clears the moment the robot moves again or the
51	blockage ends; an uninterrupted wait whose blocking robot merely changes
52	identity keeps accumulating with the new blocker, whereas a wait that was
53	interrupted and later recurs starts again at one. An accepted map edit
54	reconciles the records immediately: a robot paused by the new map or no
55	longer facing its recorded blocker on the replanned route loses its entry, an
56	entry still facing the same blocker keeps its count, and no edit ever creates
57	or increments one.
58	
59	Initial task ownership
60	----------------------
61	A fleet can be created mid-work: a robot may already name its current task
62	with a remaining route, and a task may already be assigned or even loaded.
63	Construction validates these bindings up front instead of discovering them
64	while stepping. Every robot that names a task must name one that exists, is
65	still unfinished and is assigned back to that robot; every unfinished task
66	that names an owner must name an existing robot whose current task it is, and
67	a task with the goods collected may never lack that owner. One robot is
68	therefore never claimed by two unfinished tasks, and a robot may never be
69	bound to a completed task. Finished tasks only retain *historical* ownership:
70	their recorded robot need not be idle or name them back, may already work a
71	new task, and may even be absent from the fleet. Unassigned, not-yet-collected
72	tasks simply wait -- including ones no robot can currently reach -- and are
73	not an ownership error. Conflicts raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot
74	or task involved; nothing is rebound, unassigned or dropped, and the caller's
75	objects are left untouched. The same unfinished-task binding rules govern
76	checkpoint loading (which additionally keeps its historical-state checks).
77	
78	Every robot's remaining route is also validated as a walk on the given map,
79	whether or not the robot is bound to a task, and direct construction and
80	checkpoint recovery run the *same* :func:`_validate_route_walk` check, so the
81	walking rule is maintained in exactly one place. The route omits the robot's
82	current cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an up/down/left/right
83	neighbour of that cell and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal step
84	from the previous one; each waypoint must be in bounds and free of obstacles.
85	Diagonal steps, multi-cell jumps, two identical consecutive waypoints and a
86	first waypoint equal to the current position are all rejected, and waypoints
87	must be two plain integers (never booleans) in a list or tuple, with wrong
88	lengths or element types raising :class:`ValueError` rather than leaking
89	unpacking or hashing errors. Empty routes stay legal; a route need not be
90	shortest and may revisit cells. A route crossing another robot's current cell,
91	or several robots planning through the same cell, is not an error -- those
92	traffic conflicts are settled during execution. The direct interface keeps
93	its existing acceptance of a bound route's pickup/dropoff ordering and end
94	point; checkpoint loading additionally keeps its own stricter route checks
95	(including the task completion rules), its format and the map-paused
96	behaviour, under which a paused robot resumes with an empty route.
97	
98	Direct construction always judges every waypoint against the map handed to
99	it, so a route crossing an initial obstacle is rejected no matter the robot's
100	task state. Checkpoint recovery owns exactly one relaxation, and only for a
101	version 2 document: a robot with no bound task keeps its remaining preset
102	waypoints when a later map edit closes the cell ahead -- it simply waits
103	before it -- so such a waypoint may be blocked on the saved map provided it
104	was traversable on the base map, some recorded change net-closes it and it is
105	still closed at save time. The set of cells this can possibly cover is
106	derived from the already validated ``base_grid`` plus ``map_changes``, never
107	from the route itself: a base-map obstacle and any blocked cell the history
108	cannot explain stay rejected, version 1 files (which carry no history) keep
109	the old rule, and a task-bound robot never qualifies. Out-of-bounds,
110	malformed and non-adjacent waypoints are rejected for every robot either
111	way. After reopening, the restored robot keeps driving the same cells in the
112	same order: waiting neither consumes a waypoint nor adds mileage, and the
113	route is never replanned into a shortcut.
114	
115	Checkpoint file format
116	----------------------
117	``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
118	version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.
119	
120	``version``
121	    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
122	``grid``
123	    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
124	    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
125	``tick``
126	    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
127	    loading never advance this value.
128	``robots``
129	    List of robot states, each
130	    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
131	    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
132	    remaining waypoints after ``position`` (empty for a paused robot). For a
133	    taskless robot the route may head into a cell the change history has
134	    closed and the saved grid still shows blocked: the robot is simply waiting
135	    there with its preset waypoints intact, and loading restores that wait.
136	``tasks``
137	    List of task states, each
138	    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
139	    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
140	    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``.
141	``replay``
142	    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
143	    through ``tick`` and have the shape
144	    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
145	    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
146	    ``completed`` is the cumulative set of tasks finished by the end of that
147	    tick: entries must name checkpoint tasks without repeats within one frame,
148	    a recorded completion must survive every later frame, and the final
149	    frame's set must equal the tasks saved with ``completed: true``.
150	    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
151	    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
152	    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
153	    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
154	    robot positions.
155	``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
156	    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
157	    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
158	``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
159	    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
160	    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
161	    ``grid``.
162	``traffic_waits`` (optional)
163	    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
164	    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
165	    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
166	    wait counter at zero. Each entry must agree with the saved layout: the
167	    robot needs a remaining route and ``blocked_by`` must name exactly the
168	    robot occupying its next route cell -- a next cell nobody occupies, a
169	    listed blocker parked elsewhere, or extra names beside the real blocker
170	    all reject the document.
171	
172	Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
173	``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
174	baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.
175	
176	The ordinary-tick-frame rules both versions share -- the replay container is
177	a list, every frame is an object, and tick frames are numbered consecutively
178	from 1 with a well-formed payload -- are owned by the single shared
179	:meth:`FleetSimulator._iter_replay_events` scan, so they are maintained in
180	exactly one place. Each version keeps its own handling on top: version 1
181	rejects non-tick frames and fills in the missing ``type`` on a copy, while
182	version 2 dispatches event types and enforces its map-change ordering.
183	
184	Both map definitions are validated by the single shared
185	:meth:`FleetSimulator._load_map_definition` rule -- positive integer
186	dimensions, an obstacle list of integer ``[x, y]`` pairs inside the map --
187	with wording that names the map at fault, so a format or value rule is
188	maintained in exactly one place while each map keeps its own contents. The
189	cross-definition constraints (matching dimensions and a history that replays
190	``base_grid`` onto ``grid``) are checked separately and remain distinct
191	rejection reasons from a malformed definition.
192	
193	Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
194	fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
195	bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
196	mismatches, routes that cannot finish the robot's bound task, traffic waits
197	that contradict the saved robot positions and remaining routes, broken replay
198	or map-change history, a completion history that contradicts the saved task
199	states, and a history that does not reproduce the saved grid all raise
200	:class:`ValueError`.
201	
202	The single route-walk exception recovery allows is a preset-route robot that
203	is waiting out a dynamic closure. In a version 2 file a robot without a bound
204	task may keep waypoints that are blocked on the saved grid when the base map
205	had the cell open and the recorded change history explains its current,
206	still-effective closure (a cell closed and reopened before the save is open
207	again and therefore never covered). Such a robot was produced by normal
208	running -- closing a cell never strips a taskless robot of its remaining
209	route, the robot just waits before the cell -- so recovery restores it as is
210	and it drives on, same cells, same order, once the cell reopens. The
211	exemption cannot reach anything else: direct fleet construction has no
212	history and rejects routes through initial obstacles, a blocked waypoint the
213	history cannot account for (including every blocked waypoint in a version 1
214	document) is still rejected, and robots bound to a task never qualify --
215	their routes are replanned or their tasks paused at edit time and load under
216	the unchanged task rules. A robot standing on an obstacle and an out-of-map,
217	malformed or non-adjacent waypoint are rejected regardless of task state.
218	
219	A task-bound route is judged against the task's pickup state, not just for
220	walkability. For every assigned, unfinished task that is not paused by map
221	unreachability, a non-empty remaining route must end at the dropoff, and when
222	the goods are not yet collected and the robot is not already standing on the
223	pickup cell, the route must still pass through that pickup cell -- passing the
224	dropoff early changes nothing as long as the route later collects and returns,
225	and avoidance detours need not match a replanned shortest route. An empty
226	route is accepted only when a loaded robot already stands at the dropoff, or
227	when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; paused tasks keep their
228	empty-route exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not checked.
229	
230	The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
231	for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
232	cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
233	robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
234	may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
235	cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
236	fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
237	duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
238	robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
239	applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
240	robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
241	cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
242	frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
243	it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
244	"""

263	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
264	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
265	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

268	def _coordinate_pair(value: object, description: str, *, strict_list: bool) -> Position:
269	    """Validate *value* as a pair of two plain integers.
270	
271	    Booleans are rejected even though they are Python ints, and wrong lengths
272	    or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of leaking unpacking or
273	    hashing errors. This is the one coordinate-shape rule shared by every
274	    caller; the two entry points only differ in the outer container spellings
275	    they accept:
276	
277	    * strict JSON lists only (*strict_list* true, checkpoints, whose document
278	      shape is fixed and must not be relaxed because validation is shared);
279	    * lists or tuples alike (*strict_list* false, the direct Python interface,
280	      where the two spellings may be mixed freely).
281	    """
282	    if strict_list:
283	        # Checkpoints keep their single, fixed message for every shape problem
284	        # -- wrong type, wrong length or a non-integer (including a boolean) --
285	        # because the JSON document shape is fixed and shared validation must
286	        # not change what a malformed checkpoint reports.
287	        if (
288	            not isinstance(value, list)
289	            or len(value) != 2
290	            or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
291	        ):
292	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
293	    else:
294	        if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
295	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
296	        if len(value) != 2:
297	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
298	        if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
299	            raise ValueError(
300	                f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types"
301	            )

315	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
316	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
317	
318	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
319	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
320	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
321	
322	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
323	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
324	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
325	      completes anything by itself.
326	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
327	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
328	
329	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
330	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
331	    unreachable one.
332	    """
333	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
334	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
335	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
336	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
337	    if task.dropoff != last:
338	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
339	    return waypoints

342	def _plan_task_route(
343	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
344	) -> list[Position] | None:
345	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
346	
347	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
348	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
349	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
350	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
351	    """
352	    route: list[Position] = []
353	    current = origin
354	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
355	        try:
356	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
357	        except ValueError:
358	            return None
359	        route.extend(leg)
360	        current = waypoint
361	    return route

368	    *,

374	
375	    This is the single place that owns the walking rule shared by direct
376	    fleet construction and checkpoint recovery, so the same legality check is
377	    never edited twice. A route holds the cells still ahead of *origin*:
378	
379	    * every waypoint must parse as two plain integers (booleans are rejected),

381	      currently obstructed waypoint a version 2 checkpoint recovery may carry

385	    * every later waypoint must be exactly one orthogonal step from the
386	      previous one -- diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps and two identical
387	      consecutive waypoints are all rejected.
388	
389	    Detours and revisits (including *origin*) are legal, and a route crossing
390	    another robot's cell is never a walk error: traffic is settled while
391	    stepping, not here. The walkability rule deliberately says nothing about
392	    the bound task's pickup/dropoff requirements; checkpoint loading keeps
393	    that separate, stricter business check. The result is a fresh mutable list
394	    of tuple cells, so validating never aliases or mutates the caller's
395	    container and a rejected input leaves every earlier object untouched.
396	
397	    *blocked_cells* is honoured only for checkpoint recovery and names the
398	    cells the recorded map-change history explains: cells open on the base map

401	    -- the robot keeps its unconsumed waypoints and simply waits before it --

403	    deliberately narrow: only checkpoint loading ever supplies the set (direct
404	    construction leaves it ``None``), only a robot without a bound task may
405	    use it (the caller never passes the set for a task route), and the cells
406	    must be inside the map -- an out-of-bounds waypoint is rejected regardless.
407	    A blocked cell in the base map that no edit explains is never part of the
408	    set, so a route crossing an initial or unexplained obstacle stays illegal.
409	
410	    The two entries keep their existing format and wording differences via
411	    *checkpoint*: direct construction (false) accepts a list or tuple route of
412	    list-or-tuple cells and reports ``route waypoint N`` with a dedicated
413	    message for a first waypoint on the current cell and for repeated
414	    consecutive waypoints; checkpoint loading (true) keeps the strict JSON
415	    list-of-lists format (``_as_pair``), says ``route entry`` and folds both
416	    equal-cell cases into its existing non-adjacency message. The checks
417	    performed are identical either way.
418	    """
419	    allowed_blocked = frozenset() if blocked_cells is None else blocked_cells
420	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
421	    previous = origin
422	    for index, cell in enumerate(route):
423	        if checkpoint:
424	            waypoint = _as_pair(
425	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {index}"
426	            )
427	        else:
428	            waypoint = _as_cell(
429	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
430	            )
431	        if not grid.contains(waypoint) or (
432	            waypoint in grid.obstacles and waypoint not in allowed_blocked
433	        ):
434	            if checkpoint:
435	                raise ValueError(
436	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
437	                    "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
438	                )
439	            raise ValueError(
440	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
441	                f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
442	            )
443	        if waypoint == previous:
444	            if checkpoint:
445	                # The checkpoint wording treats an equal cell like any other
446	                # non-adjacent step, naming both cells of the offending move.
447	                raise ValueError(
448	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
449	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
450	                )
451	            if index == 0:
452	                raise ValueError(
453	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)} "
454	                    "is the robot's current cell; the remaining route must "
455	                    "start with the next cell"
456	                )
457	            raise ValueError(
458	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route repeats cell {list(waypoint)} at "
459	                f"consecutive waypoints {index - 1} and {index}"
460	            )
461	        if (
462	            abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
463	            + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
464	            != 1
465	        ):
466	            if checkpoint:
467	                raise ValueError(
468	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
469	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
470	                )
471	            if index == 0:
472	                segment = (
473	                    f"from its current position {list(previous)} to route "
474	                    f"waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
475	                )
476	            else:
477	                segment = (
478	                    f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} to "
479	                    f"waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
480	                )
481	            raise ValueError(
482	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently {segment}: "
483	                "every step must move one orthogonal cell"
484	            )
485	        waypoints.append(waypoint)
486	        previous = waypoint
487	    return waypoints

515	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
516	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):

518	        self._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
519	        if _routes_prevalidated:
520	            # Checkpoint recovery has already run the shared
521	            # :func:`_validate_route_walk` itself -- including its one narrow
522	            # checkpoint exemption for a taskless preset route waiting before
523	            # a history-explained closed cell -- so its already-normalized
524	            # routes must not be re-checked here against the saved grid, where
525	            # those legitimate waypoints look obstructed. Every other
526	            # constructor check above still runs.
527	            return
528	        # Accepted routes share one internal shape regardless of how the caller
529	        # spelled them: a mutable list of tuple cells. The normalized copies are
530	        # committed only after every robot passed validation, so a rejection
531	        # (even one buried in a later robot's route) never touches the caller's

537	    @staticmethod
538	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
539	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
540	
541	        The very same mutual-ownership requirement backs direct construction
542	        and checkpoint loading, so it lives in exactly one place. The binding
543	        only governs work still in progress:
544	
545	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
546	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
547	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
548	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
549	          collected additionally must have an owner.
550	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
551	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
552	
553	        Completed tasks only keep *historical* ownership: their recorded
554	        ``assigned_robot`` is not required to be idle or to name them back, so
555	        a robot that already finished one task may be idle or busy with a new
556	        one. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- even when no
557	        robot can reach them -- and are not an ownership error. Nothing here
558	        rewrites a binding or drops a task; an inconsistent input is rejected
559	        as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the conflicting robot or
560	        task, leaving the caller's objects untouched.
561	        """
562	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
563	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
564	        for robot in robots:
565	            if robot.task_id is None:
566	                continue
567	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
568	            if task is None:
569	                raise ValueError(
570	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
571	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
572	                )
573	            if task.completed:
574	                raise ValueError(
575	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
576	                    "that is already completed"
577	                )
578	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
579	                raise ValueError(
580	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
581	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
582	                )
583	        for task in tasks:
584	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are
585	            # free to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a
586	            # task is still in progress.
587	            if task.completed:
588	                continue
589	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
590	                raise ValueError(
591	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
592	                )
593	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
594	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
595	                if owner is None:
596	                    raise ValueError(
597	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
598	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
599	                    )
600	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
601	                    raise ValueError(
602	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
603	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
604	                    )

606	    @staticmethod
607	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
608	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
609	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
610	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
611	
612	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
613	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
614	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
615	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
616	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
617	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
618	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
619	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
620	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
621	
622	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
623	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
624	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
625	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
626	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
627	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
628	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
629	
630	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
631	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
632	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
633	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
634	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
635	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
636	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
637	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
638	        """
639	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
640	        for robot in robots:
641	            route = robot.route
642	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
643	                raise ValueError(
644	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
645	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
646	                )
647	            normalized.append(
648	                _validate_route_walk(
649	                    grid,
650	                    robot.position,
651	                    route,
652	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
653	                    checkpoint=False,
654	                )
655	            )
656	        return normalized

662	    def modify_obstacles(
663	        self,
664	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
665	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
666	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
667	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
668	
669	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
670	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
671	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
672	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
673	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
674	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
675	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
676	
677	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
678	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
679	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
680	        distance is accumulated.
681	        """
682	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
683	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
684	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
685	        if conflict:
686	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
687	            raise ValueError(
688	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
689	            )
690	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
691	        for cell in add_cells:
692	            if cell in occupied:
693	                raise ValueError(
694	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
695	                )
696	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)

698	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
699	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
700	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
701	        seen: set[Position] = set()
702	        ordered: list[Position] = []
703	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
704	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
705	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
706	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
707	            if position in seen:
708	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
709	                continue
710	            seen.add(position)
711	            ordered.append(position)
712	        return ordered

714	    def _apply_map_change(
715	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
716	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
717	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
718	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
719	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
720	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
721	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
722	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
723	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
724	
725	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
726	        # known to change the map.
727	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
728	        self._map_sequence += 1
729	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
730	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
731	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
732	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
733	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
734	        return copy.deepcopy(record)

736	    def _map_change_record(
737	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
738	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
739	        return {
740	            "type": "map_change",
741	            "tick": self.tick,
742	            "sequence": sequence,
743	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
744	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
745	        }

747	    def _plan_route(
748	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
749	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
750	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
751	
752	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
753	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
754	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
755	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
756	        """
757	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
758	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)

760	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
761	        for task in self.tasks.values():
762	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
763	                continue
764	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
765	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
766	                continue
767	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
768	            if route is None:
769	                robot.route = []
770	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
771	            else:
772	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
773	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
774	                robot.route = route
775	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)

777	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
778	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
779	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
780	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
781	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
782	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
783	                continue
784	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
785	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
786	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
787	                continue
788	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
789	            if route is None:
790	                robot.route = []
791	                continue
792	            robot.route = route
793	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
794	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

800	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
801	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
802	        cells: set[Position] = set()
803	        for robot in self.robots.values():
804	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
805	                cells.update(robot.route)
806	        return cells

808	    def _safe_side_cells(
809	        self,
810	        robot: Robot,
811	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
812	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
813	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
814	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
815	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
816	
817	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
818	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
819	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
820	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
821	
822	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
823	          skips anything else),
824	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
825	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
826	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
827	          route is excluded), and
828	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
829	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
830	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
831	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
832	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
833	
834	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
835	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
836	        """
837	        blocked = set(forbidden)
838	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
839	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
840	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
841	                continue
842	            yield cell

844	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
845	        self,
846	        blocker: Robot,
847	        requester: Robot,
848	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
849	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
850	    ) -> Position | None:
851	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
852	
853	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
854	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
855	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
856	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
857	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
858	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
859	        """
860	        return next(
861	            self._safe_side_cells(
862	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
863	            ),
864	            None,
865	        )
866	
867	    def _self_sidestep(
868	        self,
869	        robot: Robot,
870	        task: Task | None,
871	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
872	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
873	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
874	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
875	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
876	
877	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
878	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
879	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
880	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
881	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
882	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
883	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
884	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
885	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
886	        """
887	        if task is None or task.completed:
888	            return None
889	        destination = robot.route[0]
890	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
891	        if blocker_id is None:
892	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
893	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
894	        best_length = 0
895	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
896	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
897	        # that order as the tie break.
898	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
899	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
900	            if route is None:
901	                continue
902	            if (
903	                blocker_id is not None
904	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
905	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
906	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
907	                )
908	            ):
909	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
910	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
911	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
912	                continue
913	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
914	                best = (cell, route)
915	                best_length = len(route)
916	        return best
917	
918	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
919	        self,
920	        robot: Robot,
921	        side: Position,
922	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
923	        blocker_id: str,
924	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
925	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
926	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
927	    ) -> bool:
928	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
929	
930	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
931	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
932	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
933	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
934	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
935	        never rejected here.
936	        """
937	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
938	            return False
939	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
940	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
941	            return False
942	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
943	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
944	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
945	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
946	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
947	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
948	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
949	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
950	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
951	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
952	        return not self._can_vacate(
953	            blocker,

984	    def _can_vacate(
985	        self,
986	        blocker: Robot,
987	        requester: Robot,
988	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
989	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
990	        checking: frozenset[str],
991	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
992	    ) -> bool:
993	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
994	
995	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
996	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
997	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
998	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
999	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
1000	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
1001	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots already on the
1002	        dependency chain (including robots that used their one move of this
1003	        tick), so meeting one again closes a cyclic dependency -- a head-on
1004	        deadlock, or the requester itself -- and never proves an exit merely
1005	        because every robot on the cycle still carries a route.
1006	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
1007	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
1008	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
1009	        the blocker's own route does).
1010	
1011	        A task-bound blocker's own side step is judged by the same standard as
1012	        the requester's retreat: it counts as leaving only when the replanned
1013	        route from the side cell does not lead straight back through the cell
1014	        being vacated into another robot that cannot get out of the way
1015	        either. A side cell the blocker must leave again on the next tick to
1016	        re-face the very same unyielding jam further down the corridor is no
1017	        way out, so it never justifies the retreat behind it.
1018	
1019	        The follow chain can run through an arbitrarily long legal queue, so
1020	        the search is an explicit stack rather than Python recursion: a queue
1021	        of twelve hundred robots ending at a parked robot with no side cell
1022	        must report "cannot vacate" from a normal ``step()`` instead of
1023	        raising :class:`RecursionError`. Each frame is
1024	        ``(robot, occupied, checking, blocked_path, resume)``: a nested
1025	        hypothetical (the blocker having stepped aside) works with its own
1026	        layout and no-go cells, so both travel with the frame. *resume* is
1027	        ``None`` on a frame's first visit and afterwards holds the robot's
1028	        not-yet-tried side-exit candidates as a stateful iterator. A frame
1029	        examined for the first time first tries the free-waypoint and
1030	        follow-chain rules; only when the chain ahead comes back empty does it
1031	        resume at its own side-cell scan, continuing exactly where that scan
1032	        stopped -- the order the single recursive call imposed.
1033	        """
1034	        frame = (blocker, occupied, checking, blocked_path, None)
1035	        stack: list[
1036	            tuple[
1037	                Robot,
1038	                dict[Position, str],
1039	                frozenset[str],
1040	                frozenset[Position],
1041	                Iterator[tuple[Position, list[Position]]] | None,
1042	            ]
1043	        ] = [frame]
1044	        while stack:
1045	            current, cur_occupied, cur_checking, cur_blocked_path, resume = stack.pop()
1046	            if current.robot_id in cur_checking:
1047	                # The chain has folded back onto a robot it already depends
1048	                # on: a cycle cannot vacate itself. The frame that followed
1049	                # this one simply resumes with its own side-cell options.
1050	                continue
1051	            task = self.tasks[current.task_id] if current.task_id is not None else None
1052	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1053	                continue
1054	            if not current.route:
1055	                if task is not None:
1056	                    # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
1057	                    # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
1058	                    continue
1059	                # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
1060	                # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
1061	                # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
1062	                # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
1063	                # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
1064	                # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
1065	                side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(current, requester, cur_occupied, reserved)
1066	                if side is not None and side not in cur_blocked_path:
1067	                    return True
1068	                continue
1069	            if resume is None:
1070	                ahead = current.route[0]
1071	                if (
1072	                    self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1073	                    and ahead not in cur_occupied
1074	                    and ahead not in reserved
1075	                ):
1076	                    return True
1077	                occupant_id = cur_occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
1078	                if (
1079	                    occupant_id is not None
1080	                    and occupant_id != current.robot_id
1081	                    and occupant_id not in cur_checking
1082	                ):
1083	                    # The robot could follow the occupant once that robot
1084	                    # vacates its cell this same tick. This frame resumes with
1085	                    # its side-cell scan only after the chain ahead proves it
1086	                    # cannot clear, mirroring the recursive call order.
1087	                    stack.append(
1088	                        (
1089	                            current,
1090	                            cur_occupied,
1091	                            cur_checking,
1092	                            cur_blocked_path,
1093	                            self._side_exit_cells(
1094	                                current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
1095	                            )
1096	                            if task is not None
1097	                            else iter(()),
1098	                        )
1099	                    )
1100	                    stack.append(
1101	                        (
1102	                            self.robots[occupant_id],
1103	                            cur_occupied,
1104	                            cur_checking | {current.robot_id},
1105	                            cur_blocked_path,
1106	                            None,
1107	                        )
1108	                    )
1109	                    continue
1110	                resume = (
1111	                    self._side_exit_cells(
1112	                        current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
1113	                    )
1114	                    if task is not None
1115	                    else iter(())
1116	                )
1117	            if task is None:
1118	                # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
1119	                # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
1120	                # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
1121	                continue
1122	            # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
1123	            # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
1124	            # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
1125	            chained = False
1126	            for side_cell, route in resume:
1127	                if not route or route[0] != current.position:
1128	                    # A genuine exit: the robot drives on elsewhere instead of
1129	                    # returning onto the cell it just vacated.
1130	                    return True
1131	                # The replanned route leads straight back through the cell
1132	                # being vacated. That still counts as leaving when the way
1133	                # back is clear, or when whoever holds it can clear out in
1134	                # turn -- but not when the robot would re-face a jam that has
1135	                # no exit of its own, because then the side step is undone on
1136	                # the next tick with nothing gained.
1137	                hyp_occupied = dict(cur_occupied)
1138	                del hyp_occupied[current.position]
1139	                hyp_occupied[side_cell] = current.robot_id
1140	                holder_id: str | None = None
1141	                for cell in route[1:]:
1142	                    holder = hyp_occupied.get(cell) or reserved.get(cell)
1143	                    if holder is not None and holder != current.robot_id:
1144	                        holder_id = holder
1145	                        break
1146	                if holder_id is None:
1147	                    return True
1148	                if holder_id in cur_checking:
1149	                    continue
1150	                stack.append(
1151	                    (current, cur_occupied, cur_checking, cur_blocked_path, resume)
1152	                )
1153	                stack.append(
1154	                    (
1155	                        self.robots[holder_id],
1156	                        hyp_occupied,
1157	                        cur_checking | {current.robot_id},
1158	                        frozenset(route),
1159	                        None,
1160	                    )
1161	                )
1162	                chained = True
1163	                break
1164	            if chained:
1165	                continue
1166	        return False

1168	    def _update_traffic_waits(
1169	        self,
1170	        waited: dict[str, str],
1171	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
1172	    ) -> None:
1173	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
1174	
1175	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
1176	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
1177	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
1178	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
1179	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
1180	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
1181	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
1182	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
1183	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
1184	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
1185	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
1186	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
1187	        """
1188	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1189	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
1190	        for robot_id in waited:
1191	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
1192	                continue
1193	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1194	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1195	                continue
1196	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
1197	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1198	                continue
1199	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
1200	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
1201	                continue
1202	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
1203	            if entry is None:
1204	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
1205	            else:
1206	                surviving[robot_id] = {
1207	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
1208	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
1209	                }
1210	        self._traffic_waits = surviving

1212	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
1213	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
1214	
1215	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
1216	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
1217	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
1218	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
1219	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
1220	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
1221	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
1222	        """
1223	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}

1226	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1227	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
1228	                continue
1229	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
1230	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]

1250	        a taskless robot still driving a preset route keeps that route and is

1253	        route either. Skipping such a robot never touches its position,
1254	        mileage, cargo state or remaining waypoints, and never makes other
1255	        tasks wait: the next available robot is chosen by the usual shortest
1256	        feasible route length with the robot id string as tie break.

1272	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)

1301	            del occupied[robot.position]

1310	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
1311	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
1312	                continue

1329	                        robot.route = route
